title: Sales Enablement: Prospect Comprehensive Playbook — Positioning, Pricing, Competitive Briefs, Case Studies & Security FAQ
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This playbook gives AEs, SDRs, and solution engineers a single, polished reference for prospect conversations that covers product positioning and messaging, short competitive briefs, a pitch-deck outline, pricing guidance, representative case studies, and a security FAQ tailored for evaluation. Use this during discovery, demo prep, and procurement conversations.

Key outcomes for reps:
- Communicate Redwood Inference's differentiated value (production-first inference economics).
- Handle common competitive and pricing objections quickly.
- Surface security and deployment controls that enterprise buyers request.
- Accelerate deal cycles with clear next steps, assets, and ownership.

1) Positioning & Messaging (1-minute / 5-minute / deep)

One-line (elevator):
Redwood Inference provides predictable, high-performance LLM inference with unified tooling across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — so engineering teams deliver low latency, low-cost, and reliable AI features without building their own serving stack.

1-minute pitch (what to say in discovery):
- Problem: LLM features are easy to prototype but expensive and fragile at production scale (latency, cost, reliability, and compliance gaps).
- Solution: Redwood provides a production-first inference runtime plus orchestration and observability across Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private deployments — letting teams trade off latency, cost, and isolation with minimal engineering effort.
- Evidence: We publish model performance profiles, provide reserved capacity (SLA-backed), and have enterprise customers running multi-region private deployments.

5-minute pitch (key points and proof):
- Serving runtime: GPU-optimized inference with batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization-aware execution to reduce per-token cost.
- Unified API & Tooling: Same REST/SDK surface and rollouts across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private (eases dev + ops handoff).
- Cost Controls: Model recommendations, batching/caching guidance, and per-token cost reporting in Console.
- Reliability: Smart routing + automatic fallbacks keep apps available under load.
- Security & Compliance: VPC/private control plane options, KMS integrations, audit logs, and data residency controls.

Deep technical messaging (for SEs):
- Kernel selection & compilation adapt at runtime to model architecture and seq-length distribution.
- Continuous batching and KV cache management reduce latency tail and increase GPU utilization.
- Can be deployed in customer VPC/on-prem with HSM/KMS support and log forwarding for SIEM.

Recommended talk tracks by persona:
- Engineering manager: focus on latency SLOs, rollout controls, and integration velocity.
- Platform/Infra: emphasize dedicated pools, autoscaling, capacity planning, and observability.
- Security/Compliance: highlight private deployment mode, encryption, and auditability.
- Product/PM: stress iteration speed, consistent dev ergonomics, and cost visibility.

2) Competitive Briefs (quick reference)

Competitor: Cloud AI managed endpoints (hyperscaler)
- Differentiators: Redwood offers unified serving across hosted/dedicated/private, more transparent token-level cost breakdowns, and opinionated cost/performance tooling (quantization suggestions + caching).
- Common objection: Hyperscalers have deep integrations and scale — rebuttal: Redwood focuses on inference economics and predictable latency at lower operational cost; we integrate with customer clouds and support private control planes.

Competitor: LLM API providers (simplicity-first)
- Differentiators: Production SLOs, reserved capacity, and private deployments for regulated workloads.
- Objection: They are easier for prototypes — rebuttal: Redwood supports quick onboarding and self-serve Hosted API while also providing the enterprise controls that large customers need.

Competitor: Self-hosted inference runtimes / OSS
- Differentiators: Managed orchestration, rollout tooling, and cost-performance recommendations.
- Objection: OSS avoids vendor lock-in — rebuttal: Redwood offers private deployment and exportable configs (model version pins, rollout policies) to minimize lock-in risk.

3) Pitch Deck (recommended 10–12 slides)

Slide flow (short note for presenter):
1. Title & Value Prop — 1-line + logo
2. Problem: production gaps (latency/cost/reliability) — empirical numbers from customer discovery
3. Redwood solution: deployment modes & unified API — diagram showing Hosted / Dedicated / Private
4. How it works: runtime optimizations, caching, routing — 2–3 bullets
5. Cost controls: batching, quantization recommendations, cost dashboards — screenshot callout
6. Reliability & SLAs: Dedicated SLAs, fallback policies, regional routing
7. Security & Compliance: VPC, KMS/HSM, audit logs, SOC-type evidence
8. Customer examples: 2 short case studies (thumbnail)
9. Pricing model & commitment options — quick grid (see Pricing Guidance)
10. Implementation & timeline — typical 4–8 week path to production for medium integrations
11. ROI / TCO snapshot — sample cost comparison vs naive self-hosting or non-optimized managed endpoints
12. Next steps & POC ask — call to action: test credits, bench eval, or dedicated pilot

Assets to include with deck:
- One-page technical diagram (PDF)
- Demo script for 20-minute product demo
- 1–pager pricing summary for procurement

4) Pricing Guidance (reps guide; not a quote)

Pricing models we offer (summary):
- Hosted API (usage-based): pay-per-token generation + embeddings, tiered volume discounts. Good for fast value and low commitment.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly/annual GPU pool commitments with SLA; best for predictable throughput and lower per-token costs.
- Private (enterprise license): platform fee + support, deployed inside customer network; pricing varies by footprint and support tier.

Quick pricing grid (example ranges — use legal-approved sheet for exact numbers):
Option: Hosted | Price Signal: $/token (variable) | Typical fit: Early/PLG, prototypes, low-SLA | Key negotiation levers: Volume tiers, burst credits
Option: Dedicated | Price Signal: $/GPU-hour reserved + $/token (discounted) | Typical fit: High-throughput product features | Key negotiation levers: Commit length (1/3 yr), autoscale burst policies
Option: Private | Price Signal: Platform fee + services | Typical fit: Regulated/air-gapped deployments | Key negotiation levers: Deployment scope, retention, support SLAs

Negotiation guidance for AEs:
1. For mid-market prospects focused on cost predictability, lead with Dedicated and 12-month commit. Offer a staged rollout: PoC on Hosted -> Dedicated pilot -> Full migration.
2. For enterprise/regulatory prospects, lead with Private: scope network, compliance artifacts, and SOW. Involve security & legal early.
3. Use credits and technical POC commitments to reduce procurement friction; attach a short implementation timeline.

Procurement play (typical timeline):
1. NDA & data handling questionnaire (1–2 weeks)
2. Pilot/POC (2–6 weeks) — define eval metrics (latency P50/P95, cost per 1k tokens, uptime)
3. Commercial terms & SOW (2–4 weeks)
4. Onboarding & rollout (4–8 weeks)

5) Representative Case Studies (short)

Case study: Customer: LexiDocs (SaaS document automation) — Mid-market
- Problem: Unreliable latency and high per-call cost when scaling summary and extraction features.
- Redwood solution: Moved generation to Redwood Dedicated, applied prefix caching and quantization profile; used cost dashboard to tune batch settings.
- Outcomes: 45% reduction in per-token cost, P95 latency improved from 1.2s to 280ms, feature rollout accelerated by 3 weeks.

Case study: FinReg Analytics (financial compliance vendor) — Enterprise, regulated
- Problem: Needed on-prem inference with audit trails and strict data residency.
- Redwood solution: Private deployment (air-gapped) with KMS integration, SIEM log forwarding, and canary rollouts.
- Outcomes: Achieved SOC-like evidence package; passed regulatory checklist; production rollout with zero customer-facing incidents in first 6 months.

6) Security FAQ for Prospects (short answers for common RFP questions)

Q: Where is customer data stored and how long is it retained?
A: Data residency depends on deployment mode. Hosted customers can choose region-level residency; Dedicated and Private deployments give explicit control. Retention defaults are 90 days for logs and 30 days for request payloads unless otherwise contracted; retention can be adjusted via SOW.

Q: Do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)?
A: Yes — Private deployments and Dedicated customers can integrate with their KMS/HSM for encryption-at-rest keys and key rotation policies.

Q: How do you handle audit logging and SIEM integration?
A: We provide structured audit logs (API calls, model versions, rollout events) and log-forwarding integrations (syslog, S3, or direct SIEM connectors). Logs can be retained per contract.

Q: Can Redwood operate in an air-gapped environment?
A: Yes — we offer an on-prem package for air-gapped deployments, including offline installer artifacts and a private control plane. This is scoped per customer.

Q: What certifications / compliance artifacts are available?
A: We publish SOC2 Type II summary and can provide compliance questionnaires; full evidence packets are provided under NDA for enterprise customers.

Q: How do you prevent model/regression quality issues during rollouts?
A: Our Console supports canary rollouts, A/B tests, automatic fallback policies, and integration with evaluation harnesses to run prompt-based regression checks before a rollout.

7) Sales Playbook: Demo & Objection Handling (step-by-step)

Pre-demo checklist:
- Confirm persona and success metrics (latency, cost, accuracy).
- Provision demo tenant: choose Hosted or Dedicated preview.
- Prepare 2 prompts representative of the prospect workload.

20-minute demo script (recommended):
1. 2 min intro & problem framing
2. 5 min solution overview + diagram of deployment modes
3. 8 min live demo (console: route, model switch, cost dashboard; API: 1 example generation and 1 embedding)
4. 3 min next steps & POC ask

Common objections & short responses:
- Objection: "We already have a cloud provider endpoint." Response: Acknowledge and ask about unit economics and SLA gaps; highlight dedicated capacity and tooling for lowering per-token costs and improving latency predictability.
- Objection: "We are worried about lock-in." Response: Explain private deployment options, version pinning, and exportable configs; emphasize migration patterns and short pilot approach.
- Objection: "We need strict data residency." Response: Walk through Private and region-level Hosted options, and reference the FinReg Analytics case study.
